additional_units.role_evidence_quote: Non-anastomotic biliary strictures (NAS) are a major complication after liver transplantation and occur in 29% of patients receiving a DCD donor graft, compared to 11% among recipients of donation after brain death (DBD) liver grafts in the University Medical Center Groningen (unpublished data).
additional_units.result_quote: Non-anastomotic biliary strictures (NAS) are a major complication after liver transplantation and occur in 29% of patients receiving a DCD donor graft, compared to 11% among recipients of donation after brain death (DBD) liver grafts in the University Medical Center Groningen (unpublished data).

additional_units.role_evidence_quote: The primary endpoint is the incidence of symptomatic NAS at six months after DCD liver transplantation.
additional_units.result_quote: The incidence of NAS was 29% after DCD liver transplantation and 11% after DBD liver transplantation in patients transplanted in the UMCG from 2008 to 2013 (unpublished data).

additional_units.role_evidence_quote: The study is powered to detect a clinically relevant difference in incidence of NAS between the two study groups.
additional_units.result_quote: This incidence is similar to that reported by Abt et al. (27% in DCD versus 2% in DBD transplantation), Dubbeld et al. (24% versus 8%), Croome et al. (22% versus 4%), and Meurisse et al. (33% versus 12%) [ 6 , 34 - 36 ].

additional_units.role_evidence_quote: The primary objective is to study the efficacy of end-ischemic DHOPE in reducing the incidence of symptomatic NAS after DCD liver transplantation.
additional_units.result_quote: We aim to reduce the incidence of NAS after DCD liver transplantation with DHOPE to the level observed after DBD liver transplantation (absolute difference of 29-11 = 18%).

additional_units.role_evidence_quote: We base this presumed reduction on our results in the pilot study in which 1 of 10 (10%) of the patients with a DHOPE treated liver developed NAS.
